verification.notes: Maxfield's published statement said radar services with air traffic control were terminated by mutual agreement near a non-towered airport; it did not say the aircraft received permission to switch off its transponder. The FAA distinction reported by the transportation secretary is explicit: ending radar services does not mean disabling the transponder, and the FAA said the transponder remained on. This directly contradicts the statement's paraphrase and claimed contradiction.

verification.notes: No reliable source reviewed substantiates that Derek or Shelaine Maxfield operated a sex-trafficking organization. Public material identifies Shelaine Maxfield as founder of Saprea, a nonprofit providing resources to survivors of child sexual abuse. That contrary public description undercuts the accusation but, under the strict false standard, absence of public criminal evidence is not enough to prove a universal negative.

records.text: Owens said Derek Maxfield claimed air traffic control agreed the aircraft could stop transponding, while Kash Patel said it never stopped transponding; Owens said she did not know which account was true.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It went to Page, Arizona, and it appeared that the ADS-B transponder turned off. Now, what Kash Patel told us is different from what Derek Maxfield told us. Derek Maxfield on Instagram clarified that the Air Traffic Control Center was in agreement with them that they could stop transponding. Kash Patel says that plane never stopped transponding. So I don't know what the truth is, and I'm not even pretending that we're ever gonna get the truth.

verification.notes: Patel's public statement is independently documented: after interviews with the pilot and consultation with the FAA, he said the transponder was not turned off and attributed the apparent gap to incomplete rural coverage. The accessible record did not independently preserve Maxfield's reported Instagram wording that air traffic control agreed the aircraft could stop transponding. Owens's contrast and caveat are accurately transcribed, but only one side is externally authenticated.
